content: The frameless intrauterine device (IUD), known as GyneFix, differs from the classical IUD by eliminating the rigid frame. Instead, it is anchored in the uterus by securing one end of a nylon thread into the fundal myometrium, with copper sleeves attached to the thread. This review aimed to evaluate whether the frameless IUD reduces the risks of expulsion and unintended pregnancy, as well as the incidence of bleeding and pain that might necessitate early removal. The researchers conducted a comprehensive search of databases, including the Cochrane Controlled Trial Register, MEDLINE, and Popline, covering studies from 1980 to March 2004. They also reviewed reference lists of relevant articles. Randomized trials comparing the frameless IUD to the classical framed IUD for contraception were selected for analysis. Data extraction was performed independently by two authors, and additional information was obtained from study authors when necessary. Cumulative rates for outcomes were calculated at yearly intervals, and statistical methods were used to combine trial results and assess heterogeneity. The review included four trials involving a total of 5,939 women who were randomized to either the frameless IUD or the TCu380 device. The largest trial provided data for up to eight years, with a combined total of 23,180 years of contraceptive experience. Nulliparous women were excluded from all but one small trial. In the earlier trials, which used a prototype introducer for the frameless IUD, the expulsion rate at one year was significantly higher compared to the classical device (relative risk 2.48, 95% confidence interval 1.89 to 3.26). However, in the large WHO trial, conducted between two and six years of use, the frameless IUD demonstrated a lower risk of pregnancy compared to the classical device (relative risk 0.53, 95% confidence interval 0.32 to 0.91). A more recent trial using GyneFix with a modified introducer showed no statistically significant differences in early expulsion or pregnancy rates when compared to the classical device. Additionally, the rates of removal due to excessive bleeding and/or pain were similar between the two devices (relative risk 0.92, 95% confidence interval 0.74 to 1.14 at one year; relative risk 1.13, 95% confidence interval 0.93 to 1.37 at six years). There was a slight trend toward fewer removals for pain in the early years of use, but no significant difference was observed at six years (relative risk 1.13, 95% confidence interval 0.93 to 1.37). The authors concluded that there is insufficient evidence to confirm that the modified introducer used with GyneFix has resolved the issue of early expulsions. Beyond this, the frameless IUD performs comparably to the TCu380 device and appears to have a slightly lower pregnancy rate in later years, although the absolute difference is minimal.
